title: Tech Note: Detecting Compiled Mode Runtime Errors
author: ACI US Technical Support

historical_commentary.text: This note explains that certain 4D runtime errors (such as a type mismatch in an EXECUTE command's parameters) only manifest after compilation, since the interpreter is more permissive about types than compiled code, and describes a workaround technique using typed process variables in the debugger to simulate and catch these errors before compiling. Modern 4D's compiler produces detailed, specific type-mismatch diagnostics directly at compile time, and the language itself has moved toward much stricter, more consistent typing across interpreted and compiled modes, making this manual pre-compilation error-simulation workaround largely unnecessary today, though the underlying caution about interpreted/compiled behavioral differences remains a valid general principle.
related_updates: Modern 4D compiler diagnostics report specific type-mismatch and other compiled-mode errors directly with clear messages, reducing the need for developers to manually simulate them beforehand
4D's type system has become significantly stricter and more consistent between interpreted and compiled execution in current versions, narrowing the class of errors that only appear after compiling

The EXECUTE command itself, central to the example in this note, is a legacy dynamic-code-execution command; modern 4D projects favor more structured approaches where such dynamic parameter-type mismatches are less common
